chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan said:
I asked him about a man who shaved his head before sacrificing (his animal). He said: There is no harm, and there is nothing upon him, and he should not do it again.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is no penalty or expiation upon him
key_terms.وَلَا يَعُودَنَّ: And he should not do it again (indicating dislike/disapproval)
key_terms.يَضْحَىٰ: To perform the sacrifice (Qurbani) during Eid al-Adha

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim or person shaving their head before sacrificing their animal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that shaving the head prior to the Eid al-Adha sacrifice is permissible and carries no expiation, countering stricter views that might impose a penalty. The phrase 'wa la ya'udanna' (and do not repeat it) indicates that while valid, it is considered *makruh* (disliked) to perform the act before the slaughter, emphasizing the proper sequence of rituals as a mark of reverence. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of ritual acts while maintaining the sanctity of their prescribed order.
